assumptions: The target operator has a covered battery supplier or model approaching a real procurement approval decision before the 2027 deadline.
The operator can lawfully authorize access to the relevant documents and will enforce evidence requests against suppliers; the venture itself has no direct supplier right.
The signed pack records evidence status and gaps rather than transferring statutory responsibility or guaranteeing legal compliance.
AI can accelerate extraction, mapping, and exception triage, but source authenticity, regulatory interpretation, and final QA still require accountable human review.
Fixed pricing can be protected by explicit document, revision, supplier-response, and correction limits; this has not yet been demonstrated in a paid engagement.
Optional annual support and repeat supplier or model work are not treated as retained revenue until observed.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Several deposit-paying pilots in one narrowly defined battery segment should demonstrate that operators insert the gate before approval, suppliers produce usable evidence, delivery and exception hours remain within scope, fully loaded contribution margin is attractive, a laboratory or adviser channel converts economically, and customers return for additional suppliers, models, or annual support.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Moving the intervention upstream to supplier or model approval targets the moment incomplete evidence becomes costly and avoids competing as another end-to-end passport host. The platform-neutral acceptance pack is a coherent wedge, although the workflow remains observable and reproducible.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Preventing an incompletely evidenced supplier or model from crossing procurement approval addresses a concrete risk before the 2027 mandate. The responsible operator and purchase trigger are clear, but no smaller operator is shown to have budgeted or paid for a separate pre-procurement acceptance sprint rather than using internal staff, public tools, or its DPP vendor.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A 50% deposit, fixed deliverable, no per-unit hosting, and explicitly bounded post-delivery support improve cash conversion and reduce capital, infrastructure, and lifetime-liability exposure. Economics remain service-heavy: acquisition cost, exception hours, realized pricing, partner share, contribution margin, repeat frequency, support renewal, operating leverage, and owner earnings are unmeasured.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: The procurement event narrows the use case more effectively than a general passport platform, and smaller operators may lack internal data-governance capacity. The segment still spans multiple battery categories and markets, and neither the reachable account count nor the share with a distinct pre-approval budget is established.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Customer-hosted, platform-neutral delivery can appeal to operators that want flexibility and focused supplier evidence work. Domination potential is limited because the operator owns the approval decision, the agreement is nonexclusive and replaceable, and DPP platforms, ERP vendors, and certifier alliances can add or bundle the same check.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Winning an account could lead to further suppliers, models, material changes, optional workflow support, and similar evidence-acceptance work in adjacent regulated products. Expansion is less automatic than hosted per-unit revenue, and customer-controlled workspaces plus data-use restrictions constrain cross-customer compounding.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Customer-specific applicability mappings, review history, and exception playbooks may shorten later cycles and create modest workflow familiarity. Public guidance, free test scenarios, portable outputs, nonexclusive access, restricted data reuse, and easy incumbent bundling prevent those assets from forming a durable moat without a controlled channel or trusted standard.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The offer is simpler and lower-commitment than buying a full platform: it is fixed-scope, customer-hosted, platform-neutral, deposit-funded, and stops before registry and lifetime hosting. No evidence yet quantifies superior speed, cost, acceptance accuracy, supplier response, or avoided loss, and established providers already cover evidence and validation workflows.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Operators approaching supplier and model decisions shortly before the February 2027 deadline have reason to act now, and evolving guidance makes structured preparation valuable. Undefined battery registry semantics create implementation uncertainty but matter less to this version because it stops before registration.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Independent laboratories and import advisers encounter the relevant buyer near a real compliance event, and direct technical outreach is feasible without a camera-led brand. No partner commitment, conversion, CAC, sales cycle, or lead volume is evidenced, while established certifier-platform alliances may prefer their own bundled workflow.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A single bounded pilot, customer-controlled workspace, 30,000 PLN capital hypothesis, and no continuous hosting fit the founder's skills, capital, and five-hour daily constraint materially better. Execution still depends on operator enforcement, authentic supplier inputs, careful scope control, security, legal updates, professional-liability boundaries, and eventual analyst delegation.

highest_value_structural_change: Concentrate on one battery category and secure a co-delivery agreement with a credible independent laboratory or import adviser that makes the evidence pack a standard precursor to its own testing or compliance engagement; this would improve trust, repeatable distribution, scope discipline, and workflow control without sacrificing portability.
main_structural_strength: The version ties payment to a high-consequence procurement decision and produces portable customer-owned output while deliberately excluding registry submission and long-lived hosting, making the first test capital-light, bounded, and compatible with the founder's constraints.
primary_score_limiter: The acceptance gate is only a proposed, nonexclusive, customer-controlled workflow position, so the venture lacks durable control and must prove that a labor-intensive standalone check can be acquired and repeated profitably despite public tools and incumbent bundles.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Established specialists already solve upstream evidence work, and the Bureau Veritas-Circulor offer combines trusted testing, certification, verification, traceability, completeness checks, and passport implementation. This shows that the proposed referral channel and evidence-acceptance function can be bundled by providers with stronger trust and distribution.
